newsitem.title: JAPAN: Some firms suspend business with Nomura Securities.
newsitem.headline: Some firms suspend business with Nomura Securities.

text.p: Some investment management companies said they would suspend business dealings with Nomura Securities Co Ltd from Monday following news that two of its directors were involved in suspected illegal deals.
Nomura group unit Nomura Investment Management Co Ltd said it would suspend its business with the brokerage from Monday.
Daiwa International Capital Management Co Ltd, a unit of the Daiwa Securities Co Ltd group, also said it would halt its business with Nomura from Monday.
Neither company said how long the suspension would last.
Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Sunday that an investment management unit of Nikko Securities Co Ltd had also decided to suspend its business with Nomura from Monday.
California Public Employee Retirement System (Calpers), the largest pension fund in the United States, is considering doing the same, the newspaper said.
Some institutional investors may also stop dealing with Nomura, the paper said.
A Nomura spokesman said he could not comment on the reports. "Nomura does not comment on what other companies do," he said.

Nomura said last week that the two Nomura directors involved in the suspect deals apparently made discretionary transactions and moved profits raised from Nomura's own funds to a corporate customer's account, actions which are against the law.
